Web design for Columbia businesses starts with one detail: there are several Columbias, and this page is about Columbia, South Carolina. It is a capital city, a college town and an Army town at once, and each of those brings people who have never been inside your door and decide from their phones. A restaurant, a hotel, a barber or a repair shop that shows up clearly in those searches gets the call.

Maurice Johnson writes each site by hand and builds you a free demo first. The price is printed and paid once.

Web design Columbia SC businesses need around Fort Jackson

Fort Jackson is the Army's largest initial-entry training center. The Army says it trains about half of the soldiers who enter the service each year, roughly 35,000 in basic combat training and another 8,000 in advanced individual training. Basic training lasts ten weeks, and graduations are held nearly every week: the Army describes a weekly basic training graduation, and Columbia's visitors bureau has described families arriving for Thursday morning ceremonies.

Every class that finishes means relatives traveling to see a graduation. Many arrive from other states, stay a night or two and look for somewhere to eat, sleep, get a haircut or fix a flat. They do not know Columbia. They search, compare the first few results and pick one.

Those visitors want plain answers: are you open on the days they are in town, can they make a reservation for a group of eight, how far are you from the post, is there parking for a big vehicle. A site that answers that in the first screen is doing its job.

What a visiting family checks before choosing

  • Hours for the exact days they are here, including any special graduation-week hours.
  • A tap-to-call button and an address that opens in their map app.
  • Whether you take groups, reservations or walk-ins.
  • Rough prices, or at least a menu or a service list they can scan.
  • Photos of the real place, so they know they have arrived.

None of that needs a large site. The Starter package covers it in five pages, with Google Maps and hours on the page.

Website design Columbia SC can use beyond the base

The rest of the year belongs to everyone else: students and staff at the University of South Carolina, state employees downtown, and neighbors who just need a plumber. The places they mention in a search are the ones a local site should name honestly, such as the Vista, Main Street, Five Points, Devine Street and Forest Acres. The visitors bureau points to Five Points, near the university, for boutique shopping, restaurants and nightlife, and the Vista is known as the city's arts and entertainment district.

A Five Points bar and a Forest Acres insurance agent have little in common, and their sites should not read alike either. The bar wants event nights and late hours on top. The agent wants a calm page about the kinds of policies she writes and an easy way to request a quote. Columbia web design that fits both owners comes from asking what each one sells, not from a shared template.

Google ranks local results by relevance, distance and prominence. Naming the neighborhoods you truly serve, and keeping your Google Business Profile current, helps with the first two. The Pro package includes Google Business Profile setup.

Web design Lexington SC owners can see first

Columbia itself spills over the county line: the city is the seat of Richland County, and part of it reaches into Lexington County. The towns of Lexington and Irmo have their own customers, many of whom never drive downtown for an everyday errand. A Lexington business that only says "Columbia area" leaves those nearby searchers to someone who named the town.

If you serve both sides, Pro's ten city pages let you write one page per town. Agency goes further, starting with keyword research across your whole service area before any page is written.

Columbia help that costs nothing

The South Carolina Small Business Development Center network is run from the state director's office at the University of South Carolina's Darla Moore School of Business. Its Columbia Area SBDC works from the USC Columbia Technology Incubator on Laurel Street. SBDC consultants give free, confidential advice on topics from starting a business and financing to marketing and bookkeeping, and they also help owners pursue government contracts.

If you are still writing a business plan or sorting out a loan, start there. When it is time for the website, we can show you a demo in the meantime.

Common questions

Which Columbia is this page about?

Columbia, South Carolina: the state capital, home of the University of South Carolina and of Fort Jackson. Searches for web design in Columbia also pull up results for Columbia, Missouri and other cities with the same name. Our packages and prices are the same everywhere, but the local details on this page are about the South Carolina city.

How much does website design in Columbia, SC cost?

Quotes vary a lot with who builds the site and how custom it is. Ours do not vary: Starter is $497, Pro is $997 and Agency is $1,997, each one payment. After launch, hosting, maintenance and updates cost $49 a month, or nothing extra while you keep the AI agent. You see a free demo before you decide.

Do you offer web design in Lexington, SC?

Yes. A business in Lexington, Irmo or anywhere else around Columbia gets the same process. If you serve several of those towns, the Pro package includes ten city pages, each one researched and written about that place, so a Lexington customer reads about Lexington.

Can a restaurant or hotel near Fort Jackson change its site for graduation weeks?

Yes. A notice area at the top of the home page can carry special hours, a reservation note or a family-weekend menu, and come down afterward. On our hosting plan, you ask and we make the change. There is no extra charge for routine updates while you are on hosting.

Is there a Columbia web design company with a local office I can visit?

Not ours. Dominion Web Design Pro is Maurice Johnson in Big Sandy, Texas, and every site is built remotely. You can call (903) 636-7511 any hour; an AI receptionist answers and can put you through to Maurice. Pages, demos and edits are shared by link and email.

Want to see a Columbia site before you pay for one?

Give us your business name and what you do, and a demo site gets built for you to look at on your own phone. If you like it, pick a package. If you do not, you have spent nothing but the minute it took to look.
